notices.html: Luminocity Dino Safari has closed for the season: the Freehold pop-up ran July 1 through August 16 only, so skip a special trip there until it returns next summer.
Book ahead for Bellemont Farm's Sunflower Festival: advance online tickets ($19 adult, $12 kids) beat the door price ($25, $15), and the festival runs weekends, plus Labor Day, through September 13.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: apple and peach picking are still out after the spring freeze, and blackberries have likely wrapped up too, so it's more of a farm market and flower visit than pick-your-own. The Winery Weekend Music Series still runs 2 to 5pm both days if you want live music with the trip. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm what, if anything, is ready to pick.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: no fresh update is posted for this small, family-run farm, but early September usually means peaches, apples, nectarines, pears and cantaloupe for pick-your-own. Call 609-448-0629 to confirm before you head over, and note the fields close by 5:15pm.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: blackberry picking wrapped up on September 1 and apples aren't expected ready until mid-September, so the u-pick fields may be empty between crops right now. The fall festival and corn maze don't open until September 19. Call 732-329-8656 to see if anything is currently pickable.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: no change from last week, u-pick blueberry season has wrapped, though fresh and frozen berries are still sold in the farm market. The corn maze and pumpkins don't open until September 26. Call 609-758-8514 to confirm before a special trip.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: no change from last week, this year's spring freeze wiped out sour cherries, peaches, nectarines and apples, so there's no pick-your-own fruit right now, just the country store and bakery. Pumpkin picking and hayrides don't start until late September. Call 732-462-0756 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: peach picking may be winding down and apples probably haven't started yet, since fall harvest typically kicks off in mid-September. The Sunflower Celebration hayride is still likely running Thursday through Sunday, 4:30 to 6:30pm, at $1.50 a stem. Call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to check what's ready before you drive over.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: Luminocity Dino Safari has closed for the season, it only ran through August 16, so there's nothing to visit here right now. It typically returns next summer, so check back closer to then.
